# Capacitor Auth Manager — Documentation Index

> capacitor-auth-manager (v2.4.1) is a Firebase-agnostic Google authentication library for Capacitor and the web — a drop-in alternative to @codetrix-studio/capacitor-google-auth. One auth.signIn(AuthProvider.GOOGLE) call returns a Google id token on web, iOS, and Android, which you hand to Firebase. Works with React, Vue, Angular, and vanilla JS. Author: Ahsan Mahmood (https://aoneahsan.com). npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/capacitor-auth-manager. MIT-licensed.

## About

The library exposes an `auth` singleton (works like a store — no context provider needed). You call `auth.configure({ providers })` once, then `auth.signIn(AuthProvider.GOOGLE)` from any framework. The SAME call dispatches natively to GoogleSignIn on iOS, the Android Credential Manager on Android, and Google Identity Services on the web, and returns `result.credential.idToken` on every platform. You then hand it to Firebase: `signInWithCredential(getAuth(), GoogleAuthProvider.credential(result.credential.idToken))`. The package pulls in no `firebase` dependency, and persists no secrets by default; the web flow returns an id token only (no client secret, no backend required).

Status (2.4.x): GOOGLE-FIRST. Google is the only ENABLED provider (web + iOS + Android). The other 14 providers (apple, microsoft, facebook, github, slack, linkedin, firebase, magic-link, sms, email-password, username-password, phone-password, email-code, biometric) are un-registered — calling them throws `AuthErrorCode.PROVIDER_NOT_ENABLED` — and are being re-enabled one at a time. Treat every non-Google provider page as a roadmap reference, not a working feature.

Config: `auth.configure({ providers: { [AuthProvider.GOOGLE]: { clientId, serverClientId, iosClientId } } })`. `serverClientId` is the Web OAuth client id (REQUIRED on Android to return an id token). iOS needs GIDClientID in Info.plist + the reversed-client-id URL scheme; Android needs SHA-1/256 fingerprints in the console + a Google account on the device. The library validates an OIDC nonce + the id token's exp claim but does NOT verify the signature client-side — re-validate via your server or Firebase.

This `llms.txt` follows the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) spec.

- [Quick Start](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/getting-started/quick-start): configure → signIn → onAuthStateChange in 5 minutes.
- [Configuration](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/getting-started/configuration): the full AuthManagerConfig shape.

## Framework Adapters

- [Vanilla JS](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/frameworks/vanilla-js): the `auth` singleton API.
- [React](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/frameworks/react): useAuth, useAuthState, useAuthProvider, useUser, useIsAuthenticated.
- [Vue](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/frameworks/vue): useAuth, useAuthState, useUser, useAuthProvider, useAuthConfig.
- [Angular](https://capacitor-auth-manager-docs.aoneahsan.com/frameworks/angular): AuthService, AuthModule, AuthGuard, NoAuthGuard.
